ei.title: Dabbawalas: The Lunch Box Delivery Men in India
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: Dabbawalas: The Lunch Box Delivery Men in India Mumbai, India’s largest and busiest city, has a unique tradition in which people enjoy home-cooked lunches delivered from their homes. This service is carried out by dedicated people known as dabbawalas. The delivery process begins early in the morning when lunch boxes are collected by dabbawalas from homes around Mumbai by 9:00 a.m. They are then taken to the nearest train station. Each lunch box is carefully placed on the right train heading in various directions. By 12:30 p.m., the lunches have reached their destinations in Mumbai, where they are distributed to offices. The empty lunch boxes are gathered by 5:00 p.m. and returned to their original homes by following the same route in reverse. Today, about 5,000 dabbawalas work in and around Mumbai and manage about 400,000 lunch box deliveries daily. This operation runs with remarkable accuracy, achieving a 99.99% success rate, which means just one error in every six million deliveries. Dabbawalas have a simple but effective color-coding system to ensure each lunch box reaches its planned destination. Dabbawalas owe their success to an efficient organization and a strong sense of work. Accuracy is key, and their cooperation and communication allow them to function as efficiently as a well-organized machine.
